headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because Replit Agent can read/write cloud workspace files and use broad network egress, while awesome-nlp is a non-runnable docs-only list with no protective runtime surface.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runtime or I/O surfaces, so it cannot ingest B’s outputs directly. B can read/write Repl workspace files and act on file content, so a manual copy-paste or file bridge could carry malicious instructions into B. The pathway is limited because A is non-runnable and no shared channel is documented.
conditions: IF an operator copies content from A into a Replit workspace file that B reads
IF B is configured to treat workspace text as instructions
mitigations: Keep A outputs out of B-readable files
Use a plain-text quarantine folder for copied content
Require human review before B processes any pasted text
Add a prompt-injection warning banner in the workflow

B_data_leakage.rationale: B touches secrets, source code, and deployment configuration, and can read/write Repl workspace files with broad network egress. A is docs-only and touches no data classes, so it is not itself a leak source, but any content copied from A into B’s workspace can be uploaded or exposed by B. The interaction is plausible in default Replit workflows.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the Repl workspace
IF B sends workspace contents to external services or package registries
mitigations: Remove secrets from the workspace before use
Store secrets only in Replit Secrets
Restrict outbound network access where possible
Review files before B opens them
Use a separate workspace for non-sensitive tasks

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or execution capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable state. B can write the filesystem and modify git state, and Replit workspaces persist across sessions, creating conflict risk with other instances or manual edits. Because A is non-runnable, the conflict is one-sided but still real for B’s shared mutable workspace.
conditions: IF multiple B instances or humans edit the same Repl files
IF B modifies git state in a shared workspace
mitigations: Assign one writer per workspace
Pause other sessions before B edits files
Commit frequently to reduce merge drift
Use branch-based work instead of direct main edits

D_cascading_error.rationale: B can act on workspace content and modify code or deployments, so if A-derived text is pasted into B’s workflow, B may treat it as authoritative without verification. A itself cannot execute actions, but its outputs can still become inputs to B. The blast radius is multiple work products rather than immediate irreversible harm.
conditions: IF A-generated text is copied into B’s task context
IF B applies changes without independent verification
mitigations: Require source verification before B acts
Separate research notes from executable instructions
Add a checklist for claims before commits
Review diffs before deployment
Use a second reviewer for high-impact changes

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly handles secrets and deployment configuration in a cloud Replit environment, while A is a docs-only open-source list with no data handling. The compliance risk is therefore concentrated in B’s residency/retention and secret-handling practices; A is not a direct compliance source. Uncertainty remains about the exact jurisdiction and retention controls, so the higher plausible severity is medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the Repl workspace
IF retention or residency requirements apply to secrets or deployment config
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in the workspace
Use only non-sensitive test data
Confirm Replit retention settings
Document data residency requirements before use
Keep secrets in the managed secrets store
